rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God watches events; the Prophet must warn rather than compel, while God knows his labor and the disbelievers’ tricks and will deal with them as they deserve.
rows.anchor: The Prophet’s responsibility is not to force them to accept his message. He has nothing more to do than to warn them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The directive strengthens the Prophet through hardship and confines him to his prescribed duty; the sharp address targets his opponents rather than him.
rows.anchor: this directive was meant to make him stronger in his stance and make him confine his responsibilities to the circle prescribed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is framed with amazement because the fabrication charge is especially strange from people who appreciate Arabic eloquence and can compare the Qur’an with their poets and orators.
rows.anchor: people who had a deep literary appreciation and understood the finer aspects of language and thoroughly valued brevity and eloquence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the opponents truly regard their deities as God’s partners, they should enlist them to produce a rival Qur’an, whose message most threatens those deities’ sovereignty.
rows.anchor: this is the best opportunity for them to help in authoring something like the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading challenges those who claim Muhammad authored the Qur’an and falsely attributed it to God to impress people.
rows.anchor: This last part can also mean: if they are truthful in their claim that this Qur’ ān has been authored by the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fabrication charge is only an excuse to avoid belief; the accusers themselves have no real conviction that the Qur’an was fabricated.
rows.anchor: those who regarded the Qur’ ān to be fabricated did not really have any conviction in this allegation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects a gradual sequence of concessions and holds that the original challenge was to produce a book like the Qur’an; later one- or ten-sūra challenges explain how it could be met.
rows.anchor: in my opinion, the correct view is that in the very beginning, the challenge thrown to them was to produce a book like the Qur’ ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is not a generic contest for people ready to compete; since the opponents only evade the truth, it is better to make the full demand immediately than stage it gradually.
rows.anchor: Challenges are thrown to those about whom one can say that they have the courage to try and meet them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s miraculous knowledge and wisdom could only have been bestowed by God, confirming its divine origin if the challenge is unanswered.
rows.anchor: the treasure of knowledge and wisdom it constitutes is one that could only have been bestowed by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unanswered challenge also entails that only God is worthy of worship: the opponents’ imagined deities should prove their power now or are useless.
rows.anchor: Thus the deities they have set up only exist in their imagination; they do not exist in reality.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing question combines exhortation with rebuke: after being given every opportunity, including their deities’ help, the opponents should accept faith if they fail.
rows.anchor: carry the element of exhortation as well that of rebuke.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh argued that the Prophet’s and his companions’ poverty disproved prophethood, while their own wealth suggested God favored them rather than threatened them.
rows.anchor: these people would use the lack of means and resources possessed by the Prophet (sws) and his companions as an argument against his prophethood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly pleasures are not rewards for good deeds; God gives them to both virtuous people and wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: the pleasures of this world are not given as a reward of good deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the Hereafter, this world itself is a baseless creation.
rows.anchor: this world is totally a baseless creation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actions focused wholly on this world are baseless even when an undertaking appears pious.
rows.anchor: whatever is done by focusing all attention on it is baseless too, even though it may seem to be a pious undertaking.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking worldly pleasures receive only what God wills and in whatever quantity divine authority and wisdom decide.
rows.anchor: those who are after the pleasures of this world are also given as much as God wants

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hereafter-directed effort counts only when done with faith, sincerity, and fitting righteous action; ostentation, shirk, and verbal claims to Paradise have no value.
rows.anchor: only that effort to seek the hereafter carries weight in the eyes of God which is done with faith and sincerity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those evading the Qur’an have extinguished their inner divine spark and cannot believe; faith belongs to those whose nature remains sound.
rows.anchor: the real ailment of those who are putting up excuses to evade the Qur’ ān is that their inner divine spark has been extinguished.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith arises when the Qur’an confirms the truths already witnessed within a person’s nature; people lacking those two testimonies are not equal to them.
rows.anchor: They think that whatever they are finding in their hearts is being reinforced by this heavenly testifier too.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative comparison suppresses parallel clauses that context supplies: people with the two testimonies cannot equal those deprived of them.
rows.anchor: parallel clauses are suppressed which are evident because of concomitant indications.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina means a clear, conclusive argument and here denotes innate guidance from God that distinguishes basic good from evil.
rows.anchor: this innate guidance from God is meant to distinguish between basic good and evil.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The better one protects innate guidance, the stronger it becomes; prophets have its fullest radiance, so revelation shines as light upon light.
rows.anchor: For them, the status of divine revelation is not that of light upon darkness; rather, it is light upon light

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People accept prophetic messages in proportion to their inner spark; those who extinguish it through wrongdoing enter darkness, and the same term recurs later in Hud.
rows.anchor: The stronger this spark in a person, the more initiative he will take in accepting this message

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although bayyina is grammatically feminine, its pronoun may be masculine when the intended referent is masculine, as in this passage.
rows.anchor: A masculine pronoun can be used for them if the actual connotation of the word is masculine.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatluhu means to follow or come after; minhu refers to God, who first gives innate awareness and then presents the Qur’anic record, leaving no excuse.
rows.anchor: means “to come after or later than something.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahid refers to divine revelation, whose concrete manifestation is the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ﺷﺎﻫﺪ means the divine revelation,

rows.speaker: ‘Abdull āh ibn ‘Abb ās (rta)
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the shahid as Gabriel.
rows.anchor: ‘Abdull āh ibn ‘Abb ās (rta) is of the view

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi agrees that shahid refers to Gabriel and says revelation, Qur’an, Gabriel, and messenger differ only as terms for God’s witness.
rows.anchor: refers to Gabriel and I regard this to be correct.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expressions guidance and mercy denote the beginning and end, making the Book guidance in this life and mercy in the Hereafter for those who accept it.
rows.anchor: are actually used to refer to the beginning and the end.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ Book stands before the audience as an earlier testimony, with teachings like the Qur’an and a role as guidance and mercy.
rows.anchor: It has similar teachings and in fact exists as a guide and

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage returns to the account in Yunus that traced the Quraysh’s rejection to the challenge of monotheism.
rows.anchor: The topic discussed in these verses was also brought up in verses 17-18

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers’ testimony concerns what they taught and how their communities distorted those teachings.
rows.anchor: they will be asked what they taught and what distortion was created in these teachings by their people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed witness is the worshipped deities, although they neither requested this worship nor knew about it.
rows.anchor: these deities never asked it nor did they ever got to know about it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse is declared only after the witnesses testify against the idolaters, and it opens the way to further hardships.
rows.anchor: This curse will then open the doors to all other hardships they will face.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents deny a truth from their Lord, the Prophet should not be perplexed; most people’s disbelief explains the warning’s indirect rebuke.
rows.anchor: This is a truth and it is from their Lord but most people are not professing faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh’s deepest objection to the Qur’an was its monotheism: they resented condemnation of their deities and said whatever came to mind against it.
rows.anchor: the greatest reason behind the aversion of the Quraysh for the Qur’ ān was because of its message of monotheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who falsely claim God appointed partners face lasting deprivation because Judgment will reveal their supposed deities do not exist and they must face God alone.
rows.anchor: who can be more unjust than those who worshipped other deities and absolutely falsely claimed that God had made them their partners

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that the witnesses are messengers, whom God will ask about their teaching and their communities’ distortions on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: could be of the messengers because it is mentioned in the Qur’ ān that God will elicit the testimony of every messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that the witnesses are the deities worshipped, despite never inviting this worship or even knowing of it.
rows.anchor: It is also possible that this is the testimony of the deities which were worshipped

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that angels testify through the records of deeds they kept for each person.
rows.anchor: A third possibility is that this testimony is of the angels who keep the record of deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of God’s curse follows the testimony and opens the way to the other hardships idolaters will face.
rows.anchor: form the declaration which will be made to the idolaters after this testimony is borne.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening rhetorical question presents the false attribution of partners to God as the greatest injustice.
rows.anchor: who can be more unjust than those who worshipped other deities and absolutely falsely claimed that God had made them their partners

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The injustice also brings eternal deprivation, as their false attribution to God is exposed before their Lord.
rows.anchor: The reason it is the greatest misfortune is that this thing has become the reason for their eternal deprivation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage's testimony publicly exposes those who falsely attributed partners to God.
rows.anchor: the witnesses will bear witness that these are the ones who had fabricated a lie on God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Respite in this world is an opportunity to repent, not proof that wrongdoers escape God’s grasp; refusing it leaves them no excuse for punishment.
rows.anchor: They were actually given an opportunity to repent and reform themselves; if they do not do so, they will not be left with any excuse in being punished.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their supposed helpers cannot save them; because they blocked the path for themselves and others, they face a twofold punishment.
rows.anchor: Since they not only withheld their own selves from the path of God but also stopped others from this path, they will suffer a two-fold punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hatred kept them from listening to God and His messenger, while attachment to worldly pleasures kept them from seeing God’s signs.
rows.anchor: because of hate and aversion were not prepared to listen to the call of God and His messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who squandered their abilities on false worship destroyed themselves and will necessarily lose in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: people who wasted their abilities in this way actually destroyed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their imagined gods and the support sought from them are fabricated and useless, leaving people without insight to fail in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: all their deities will turn out to be baseless since they had actually fabricated them by imputing falsehood to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers contrast with proud polytheists: they have faith, do righteous deeds, and humbly turn to God alone, and they receive Paradise.
rows.anchor: who bent before their Lord” means to devotedly turn to him in humility while disregarding others.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind and deaf disbelievers cannot respond to the Qur’an as believers with open eyes and ears can; its message appeals to preserved reason and insight.
rows.anchor: how can the blind and deaf behave in the same way with the Qur’ ān as those who have eyes and ears.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next section narrates earlier messengers and peoples chronologically to steady the Prophet with examples of perseverance and diligence and to confront Quraysh with a precedent for their own conduct.
rows.anchor: the anecdotes of the previous messengers and their nations are narrated in a chronological sequence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier peoples treated their messengers as Quraysh treated Muhammad, then were destroyed after respite; there is no reason God would spare Quraysh the same outcome.
rows.anchor: there is no reason that God will not deal with them in the same was as He did with the previous nations.
